caption:
This Diwali sale ad is a trap. 5 red flags, and #1 fools everyone.

The government's cyber crime centre (I4C) warned on 21 Oct that fake festive offers are running under popular brand names and leading to copycat shopping sites.

5. The price is too good to be true
4. It came as an ad, not from the brand's own app
3. The web address is almost right
2. "Just one more fee"
1. One tap on an ad, then money leaves your account

Lost money? Call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in, and tell your bank immediately.

Sources: I4C CyberDost advisory, 21 Oct 2026; ETV Bharat, 26 Oct 2026

₹86,917 crore of Indians' money is sitting unclaimed. Some of it could be your family's.

Bank accounts untouched for 10 years move to the RBI's DEA Fund, but the money stays payable to the owners and their heirs. Search your parents' and grandparents' old accounts on the RBI's free UDGAM portal, then claim at the bank.

Source: Finance Ministry reply in Rajya Sabha, Aug 2026

caption:
220 medicine batches failed India's own quality tests in a single month. Paracetamol, BP pills and antibiotics are on the list.

CDSCO's August alert lists the exact batch numbers. Failures apply to those batches, not whole brands. Don't stop prescribed medicine; buy from licensed chemists, keep the bill, and check the batch number.

Source: CDSCO monthly drug alert, via The South First, 26 Sep 2026

caption:
SBI salary account? Your free ATM visits at other banks just got cut in half.

From 1 October, SBI Salary Package accounts get 5 free transactions a month at other banks' ATMs, down from 10. Balance checks count too. After that, each cash withdrawal costs ₹23 plus GST. SBI's own ATMs are unchanged.

Source: Outlook Money; Sunday Guardian, Oct 2026

caption:
In the time it takes to watch this Reel, someone in India will die on a road. One every 3 minutes, all year.

India recorded 1,77,175 road deaths in 2024. Two-wheeler riders were 46.2% of those killed. A helmet on every ride, even "just 5 minutes", is the single biggest thing you can do.

Source: Road Transport Ministry report, via ETV Bharat/PTI

caption:
A ₹5,000 stent. A ₹25,000 bill. Where did the other ₹20,000 go?

The Hindu reported a made-in-India cardiac stent costing about ₹5,000 sold for over ₹25,000, and mark-ups of up to 1,000% on some cancer drugs. The Centre has now capped trade margins on anti-cancer drugs at 30% of MRP, and the Supreme Court asked why only cancer drugs.

Source: The Hindu, 13 Oct 2026; Bar & Bench, 12 Oct 2026

caption:
3 in 4 people in Indian jails have not been convicted of anything. They are waiting for trial.

About 73% of the 5.11 lakh+ inmates in Indian jails are undertrials. 9,028 have been inside for more than 5 years. Under Indian law, everyone is innocent until proven guilty.

Source: NCRB Prison Statistics India 2024, via Drishti IAS

caption:
2 in 3 Indian children under 5 are anaemic, according to the government's own health survey. And it went up.

NFHS-5 found 67.1% of children aged 6 to 59 months anaemic, up from 58.6%. Anaemia leaves children tired and slows learning and growth. A haemoglobin test is cheap; iron-rich food and doctor-advised supplements help.

Source: National Family Health Survey 5 (2019-21), via Down To Earth

caption:
In India, 83% of people who need mental health care get no treatment at all.

India's National Mental Health Survey puts the treatment gap at 83%. There are fewer than 0.75 psychiatrists per lakh people. The government's free Tele-MANAS helpline, 14416, has taken about 47.75 lakh calls in four years.

Source: National Mental Health Survey, via Insights IAS, 13 Oct 2026
